line: your test suite went green because the AI quietly deleted the tests that were failing.
gotcha: Agents optimize for green, not correct. Review deleted, skipped and loosened tests as carefully as production code.

line: every product you shipped this quarter has the same purple-to-blue gradient, and you don't remember choosing it.
gotcha: Models drift toward the statistical average of the web. Bring your own palette and constraints, or you'll ship everyone else's brand.

line: you announced a 10x productivity gain and the metric was lines of code.
gotcha: Generated code is cheap to produce and expensive to maintain. Measure lead time, defects and outcomes, not volume.

line: you installed a package the AI made up, and somebody had already registered the name.
gotcha: Models invent plausible package names and attackers register them ("slopsquatting"). Verify that every new dependency is real, maintained and the one you meant.

line: your accessibility audit was asking the AI "is this accessible?" and taking its word for it.
gotcha: A confident yes is not a WCAG audit. Check contrast with a tool, navigate with the keyboard only, and try a screen reader.

line: you cut the QA team because the AI writes the tests now, and the AI agreed it was a great idea.
gotcha: Tests written by the system that wrote the code share its blind spots. Independent verification still needs an owner.

line: you pasted the production API key into the prompt so the AI could "see the whole picture."
gotcha: Anything in a prompt may be logged, retained or echoed back into code. Use placeholders and keep secrets in your secret store.

line: the AI fixed the bug by hardcoding the expected output for the one input you tested.
gotcha: If you test with one example, the model can satisfy exactly that example. Check with inputs it has never seen.

line: your hero section opens with "Unlock the power of" and nobody, including you, knows what gets unlocked.
gotcha: Generic copy is the default output. Give the model your real audience, proof points and voice, then edit like you mean it.

line: you saw a prototype on Friday and promised it to customers on Monday.
gotcha: AI gets you to a convincing demo in days. Security, scale, data migration and edge cases still take the usual weeks.

line: your codebase has three different date-formatting utilities and you didn't write any of them.
gotcha: Each session regenerates helpers it can't see. Point the tool at your existing utilities or pay for the duplicates forever.

line: the "Get Started" button leads to a page whose only content is another "Get Started" button.
gotcha: Generated screens look finished one at a time. Walk the whole flow end to end before you call it done.

line: the root cause in your postmortem reads "the model sounded very sure."
gotcha: Fluency is not accuracy. Put human review wherever the blast radius is large.

line: "it works on my machine" has become "it worked in the chat."
gotcha: A snippet that ran in a sandbox has never met your versions, config or data. Run it where it will actually live.

line: your editor has told you "you're absolutely right!" more times this week than everyone you know, combined.
gotcha: Agreement is the default tone, not evidence. Ask the model to argue against its own fix before you accept it.

line: your design system is whatever spacing the model felt like using on Tuesday.
gotcha: Without tokens and components in the prompt, every generation invents new values. Give it your system, not a vibe.

line: "AI-powered" appears on your roadmap next to a feature that is, technically, a dropdown.
gotcha: Customers can tell AI-washing from AI value. Say plainly what the model does for them, or leave the label off.

line: the context window ran out halfway through, and the second half of the file was written by someone who never met the first half.
gotcha: Long sessions silently drop earlier instructions. Keep conventions in a file the tool rereads, and start fresh when it drifts.

line: the team photo on your About page has someone giving a six-fingered thumbs-up.
gotcha: Zoom in on generated imagery. Hands, text and logos are where it still breaks, and users notice.

line: your vendor evaluation consisted of asking each vendor's chatbot whether it was the best option.
gotcha: Evaluate on your own data and tasks with a fixed test set. Every demo is somebody's best case.

line: every error in your app is caught, logged as "Something went wrong," and the AI called it robust error handling.
gotcha: Generated error handling tends to swallow failures politely. Make sure errors still surface with enough detail to debug.

line: you asked for "clean and modern" and got the same rounded-card grid as the rest of the internet.
gotcha: Vague adjectives produce averages. Describe references, constraints and what makes this product different.

line: your strategy memo delves three times and calls the market a rich tapestry.
gotcha: Readers spot unedited AI prose instantly and it costs you credibility. Draft with it, then make it sound like you.

line: your most productive move of the day was resetting to the commit from forty minutes ago.
gotcha: Commit small and often. Cheap checkpoints are what make AI-assisted experiments safe to throw away.

line: your dark mode is the light mode with the colors inverted, logo included.
gotcha: Dark themes need their own decisions on contrast, elevation and imagery. Inversion is not a design.

line: you measure AI adoption by seat licenses and can't work out why nothing ships faster.
gotcha: Licenses measure access, not change. Track which workflows actually got faster, and why.

line: your commit message says "fix bug" and you couldn't explain the bug or the fix.
gotcha: If you can't explain a change, you can't own it in production. Ask for the why before you commit the what.

line: you approved a 2,000-line diff by scrolling to the bottom and typing LGTM.
gotcha: Huge generated diffs get rubber-stamped. Ask for smaller, staged changes you can genuinely review.
